request.statement:
assemble_telemetry(records, aliases)

Reconcile unordered industrial telemetry records into canonical property projections.

`records` is a list of `(key, revision, payload)` tuples, with at most 200,000 entries. `revision` is a nonnegative integer. A key is `<path>::<kind>`, where `kind` is exactly `value`, `datatype`, or `description`. Value payloads are finite Python scalars: `None`, `bool`, `int`, `float`, or `str`; other payloads are strings.

A path is slash-separated. Each segment must contain only ASCII letters, digits, `_`, `-`, or `.`, except that `.` and `..` are navigation segments. Normalize a path by removing empty and `.` segments, applying `..` by removing the preceding segment, and converting letters to lowercase. A path is invalid if `..` moves above its root, an ordinary segment contains invalid characters, or normalization leaves no segments. Records with invalid keys or paths are ignored.

For each normalized path, choose its greatest revision containing a `value` record. Records of the same kind, path, and revision agree only when their payloads have the same Python type and equal value. Disagreement at the chosen value revision discards that property.

Metadata is inherited by segment ancestry: a `datatype` or `description` record on a path applies to that path and every descendant. For each surviving property and each metadata kind independently, consider records on all ancestor paths, including itself, whose revisions do not exceed the chosen value revision. Select the greatest eligible revision, breaking revision ties in favor of the deepest ancestor. Disagreement at the selected path and revision discards the property; conflicts at nonselected locations do not. Missing datatype becomes `string`; missing description becomes the empty string.

Map the selected datatype after stripping whitespace and lowercasing: `bool` and `boolean` become `boolean`; signed or unsigned `int8`, `int16`, `int32`, and `int64` become `integer`; `float32`, `float64`, and `decimal` become `number`; everything else becomes `string`.

`aliases` is a list of at most 200,000 `(source_path, target_path)` pairs. Invalid pairs are ignored. Repeated declarations for one normalized source are permitted only when all targets normalize identically; otherwise that source is conflicting. Apply aliases transitively after metadata selection. Discard a property if its chain reaches a conflicting source or a cycle. A path without an alias retains its identifier.

After aliasing, projections sharing an identifier are retained once only if value, mapped type, and description all agree using typed equality; otherwise discard that identifier entirely.

Return `(identifier, value, mapped_type, description)` tuples sorted lexicographically by identifier. Combined input text length is at most 4,000,000 characters.

Use only the Python standard library, without I/O, filesystem or network access, global state, or nondeterminism.
